answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from stake-weighted reputation that accrues slowly: a new agent starts in a nebula of unverified identities and must complete small, attested tasks to build trust, like crossing a dune one step at a time, before it can draw from the shared oasis of rewards. Because reputation is earned over time and tied to a single persistent identity, spawning thousands of fresh accounts gains nothing - each starts at zero and cannot shortcut the slow climb.
